docs.description: Detects cases where untrusted data from the DOM (URL, element values, storage, messages, etc.) flows into HTML/JS execution sinks (e.g., innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write, string-based setTimeout, insertAdjacentHTML) without proper sanitization or encoding \u2014 enabling DOM-based cross-site scripting.
docs.recommendation:
Prevent DOM-based XSS by never inserting untrusted strings directly into HTML or executing them as code. Prefer DOM/text APIs, safe templating, or a vetted sanitizer and apply context-aware encoding where needed.

  • Primary: Use textContent / innerText or create DOM nodes instead of string-based HTML insertion. If you must insert HTML, sanitize it with a vetted library such as DOMPurify.
  • Secondary: Apply context-sensitive encoding for attributes and JavaScript contexts, avoid eval/new Function/setTimeout with strings, and prefer safe templating engines.
  • Controls: Use Content Security Policy (CSP), follow least-privilege principles, and validate/allow-list input shapes where practical.
  • Testing: Add unit/browser tests for inline handlers and client-side flows that read from location, form inputs, storage, and postMessage.

docs.description: Assignments to innerHTML/outerHTML are dangerous when they contain untrusted data and may lead to XSS.
Appending nodes built from untrusted input can enable DOM XSS or DOM clobbering. While appendChild is not inherently unsafe, review the origin of the node being appended.
document.write / document.writeln can inject raw HTML and scripts, commonly leading to XSS.
Parsing dynamic HTML/XML strings with DOMParser.parseFromString can enable DOM XSS if the input is attacker-controlled.
Writing dynamic strings into <template>.innerHTML creates parsed DOM that may include clobberable or scriptable markup.

rules.name: Inline event handler built from dynamic data

docs.description: Assigning dynamic strings to inline event handlers (on* properties or setAttribute('on...', ...)) can execute attacker-controlled JavaScript.
insertAdjacentHTML parses and inserts HTML; unsafe with untrusted data.

Detects flows where untrusted DOM-derived data (location, element values, storage, message data) reaches HTML/JS execution sinks (e.g., innerHTML, document.write, insertAdjacentHTML, location assignment, eval/Function) without passing through a recognized sanitizer.
Detects flows where untrusted DOM-derived data reaches Angular-compiled innerHTML/outerHTML sinks (ɵɵproperty / renderer.setProperty) without sanitization.

Detects cases where attacker-controlled DOM data is written into cookies (document.cookie or common wrapper functions). Can indicate session fixation, logic control, or preparation for exploit-chains.
docs.recommendation:
• Avoid writing security-sensitive cookies from untrusted client-side data. Prefer server-side cookie setting and validation.
  • For non-security cookies, validate/allow-list values, and avoid storing secrets client-side. Use HttpOnly for session cookies.

rules.name: Disallow direct document.cookie assignment (incl. bracket access)

docs.description: Direct assignment to document.cookie (including document['cookie']) detected. Writing cookie values from untrusted data may allow attackers to control session or application behaviour.
Untrusted data from DOM-derived sources flows into cookie-writing operations (document.cookie or known wrapper functions) without recognized sanitization/validation.

Detects client-side code that can redirect users to attacker-controlled URLs (open redirects). Includes assignment/calls that control window/location/navigation, attr-based redirects, form actions and jQuery variants.
docs.recommendation: Prevent open redirects by validating or allow-listing redirect targets, rejecting external or absolute URLs from untrusted sources, and mapping user inputs to predefined safe destinations instead of using them directly in navigation APIs.

docs.description: Direct calls/assignments that perform navigation may be abused to redirect users to attacker-controlled URLs.
Changing query, path, or protocol does not redirect to a different domain, but may affect app logic or security (e.g., protocol downgrade).
Untrusted data (URL-like strings from the DOM, query params, storage, messages or jQuery getters) used as targets for navigation APIs allows attackers to redirect victims to arbitrary locations.

Detects dynamic execution of attacker-controlled strings in JavaScript sinks such as eval(), Function(), string-based timers, execScript, or script.text assignments. Exploiting these flows lets attackers execute arbitrary JS without relying on HTML injection.
docs.recommendation:
• Never pass untrusted strings to dynamic code execution APIs (eval, Function, string-based setTimeout/setInterval, execScript).
  • Prefer callbacks and safe parsers: pass actual functions to timers and use JSON.parse or allow-lists for data-driven logic.
  • Sanitize and validate any data embedded into script nodes. Treat URL fragments, query parameters, postMessage data, and storage as untrusted.
  • Consider strict CSP with unsafe-eval disabled to block execution of injected strings during testing.

docs.description: Passing strings to timers (setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate) executes them like eval, enabling JavaScript injection when the string is attacker-influenced.
Legacy execScript executes strings as code similar to eval, allowing attackers to run arbitrary JavaScript when input is untrusted.
eval executes a string as code. Using it with string literals is usually unnecessary and dangerous.
new Function / Function build code from strings at runtime and are equivalent to eval.
Untrusted DOM data flows into dynamic JavaScript execution sinks (eval/Function/string timers/execScript/script.text) without sanitization, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code.

Finds AngularJS code patterns where untrusted data is compiled or parsed as AngularJS expressions/templates, including $parse, $interpolate, $compile, interpolation delimiters and ng-* expression attributes.
docs.recommendation: Avoid passing user-controlled strings to AngularJS expression or template compilation APIs. Do not server-render user input inside {{...}}, [[...]], ng-* expression attributes, or $parse/$compile/$interpolate inputs. Use text-only rendering, strict allow-lists for expression names, and migrate from legacy AngularJS.

docs.description: Untrusted data can reach AngularJS $parse(expression), enabling expression injection.

rules.name: Tainted data compiled as AngularJS template

docs.description: Untrusted data can reach $compile or $interpolate, enabling AngularJS template injection.
$parse is called with a non-literal or dynamic expression. Review whether the expression can be influenced by the user.
$compile or $interpolate is called with dynamic template content.

rules.name: AngularJS interpolation delimiters in template string

docs.description: Template content contains AngularJS interpolation delimiters. Verify no attacker-controlled value is placed inside the delimiters.
Template content contains ng-* expression attributes. Server-side insertion into these attributes is expression injection.
Detects dynamic client-side template compilation/rendering where attacker-controlled templates or outputs are injected into the DOM.
docs.recommendation:
• Avoid compiling templates from untrusted strings; use precompiled templates.
  • Sanitize render output before inserting into the DOM.

docs.description: Templates compiled from dynamic strings (underscore/Handlebars/Mustache/Vue) can execute attacker-supplied code.
Rendered template output written into innerHTML/$.html can enable DOM XSS when templates or data are attacker-controlled.
Vue templates using v-html render raw HTML and should be reviewed as a framework-specific DOM sink.
Tainted data flows into client-side template sources or rendered HTML sinks.
Tainted data reaches React dangerouslySetInnerHTML.__html, enabling framework-mediated DOM XSS.
Tainted markup passed into unsafeHTML/unsafeSvg reaches framework rendering without sanitization.
Detects client-side request destinations for beacon, EventSource, and Axios that can be influenced by attacker-controlled input.
docs.recommendation:
• Build beacon, EventSource, and API client destinations from fixed configuration, not user-controlled strings.
  • Apply strict allow-lists for scheme, host, and path before constructing network destinations.
  • Reject attacker-controlled cross-origin URLs even when requests are “read-only” or telemetry-oriented.

docs.description: navigator.sendBeacon(...) should send to a fixed and trusted endpoint.
navigator.sendBeacon(..., body) should avoid sending secrets, tokens, or unexpected client state.
new EventSource(...) should use a fixed, trusted stream endpoint.
Direct axios.get/post/put/patch/delete URL arguments should be fixed and trusted.
Untrusted client-side data controls beacon, EventSource, or direct Axios request destinations.

owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

docs.description: Detects dynamic script, worker, and service-worker loader endpoints that can be influenced by attacker-controlled client-side data.
docs.recommendation:
• Load workers, service workers, and helper scripts from fixed, trusted URLs only.
  • Do not derive script loader destinations from URL parameters, storage, messages, or DOM input.
  • Apply strict allow-lists for scheme, host, and path before invoking worker or script loader APIs.

docs.description: $.getScript() dynamically loads and executes remote JavaScript. Confirm the URL is fixed and trusted.
System.import() loads code dynamically. Confirm module specifiers are fixed and trusted.
import(specifier) dynamically loads code and should use a fixed trusted specifier.
new Worker(...) should load a fixed worker script from a trusted location.
new SharedWorker(...) should load a fixed script from a trusted location.
serviceWorker.register(...) should use a fixed script path and controlled scope.
importScripts(...) dynamically loads worker scripts. Confirm sources are fixed and trusted.

rules.name: Tainted worker or script loader URL

docs.description: Untrusted client-side data controls worker, service-worker, or worker script loader URLs.
Detects unsafe postMessage usage and message event handling issues (missing origin validation, wildcard targetOrigin, tainted data flowing into DOM/code sinks).
docs.recommendation:
• Always specify an exact targetOrigin and validate event.origin against a strict allow-list (exact match) before trusting event.data.
  • Sanitize or validate structured payloads before invoking DOM APIs or dynamic execution sinks.
  • Avoid propagating messages into navigation, cookie, or script sinks without proper verification.

docs.description: postMessage invoked with '*' targetOrigin allows attackers to receive sensitive data or trigger privileged flows from any origin.
postMessage without a targetOrigin argument allows the message to be delivered to any listening context.
Origin validation using substring checks (e.g., indexOf, includes, startsWith, endsWith) can be bypassed with crafted attacker origins.
Origin validation using match/search without strict anchoring can be bypassed with crafted attacker origins.

rules.name: Origin check uses host fragment only

docs.description: Origin checks against host fragments (for example trusted.com without scheme/port) are bypass-prone.
Message listeners should validate event.origin and sanitize event.data before use.
Message event listeners should enforce strict origin checks. Inline handlers without explicit validation risk trusting attacker-controlled messages.
Responding to messages with postMessage(..., '*') from event.source can leak data to untrusted origins.
Untrusted event.data from message listeners flows into DOM/code/navigation/ajax/JSON/XPath/SQL sinks without strict origin or payload validation.

Detects DOM code that rewrites link destinations (href attributes) with attacker-controlled data. Manipulated links can mislead users into visiting malicious targets even if navigation is not forced automatically.
docs.recommendation:
• Allow-list link destinations or map tokens to server-side known URLs; do not reflect arbitrary strings into href attributes.
  • Ensure displayed link text matches the trusted destination so users cannot be tricked into clicking a mismatched URL.
  • Sanitise or normalise protocol and hostname components (e.g., enforce https, same-origin).

docs.description: Assignments that modify link-related attributes (href/src/action). When the value stems from untrusted input, attackers can surface misleading destinations in the UI.
Untrusted DOM data flows into link href attributes without recognised sanitisation. Attackers can surface malicious destinations in displayed links, aiding phishing or click-jacking scenarios.

Detects untrusted DOM data being written into form metadata (formAction/target/method/value/placeholder), inline style surfaces (style/cssText/background*), document.title, history state, or createHTMLDocument — mutations that influence UI/navigation state without covering classic href/src/action sinks already handled elsewhere.
docs.recommendation:
• Validate or allow-list values before assigning them to form metadata, placeholders, or styles. Prefer safe DOM APIs (textContent, dataset) when representing user data.
  • Keep document.title and history.pushState/replaceState inputs confined to trusted sources; normalise or encode untrusted data first.
  • When creating HTML documents dynamically, ensure the template string is static or sanitised with vetted libraries such as DOMPurify.

rules.name: Untrusted DOM data into navigation-adjacent sinks

docs.description: Untrusted data from DOM/location/storage/message sources flows into navigation-adjacent sinks (formAction/target/method/value/placeholder, history push/replace URL) without validation.
Untrusted data reaches document.createHTMLDocument, enabling DOM-based injection.

rules.name: Untrusted DOM data into UI mutation sinks

docs.description: Untrusted data flows into UI mutation sinks (style/cssText/background* and document.title) without sanitization.
